title: Operator knowledge synthesis and runbook creation playbook
author: Priya Raman
content:
Summary

This playbook codifies the process for converting incident investigations and retrospectives into operational runbooks and structured knowledge artifacts. It is intended for Platform Operators, Incident Leads, and Engineering managers who are responsible for ensuring that knowledge produced by post-incident analysis becomes runnable, testable, and discoverable runbooks.

Goals

- Ensure every Sev2+ incident has an associated runbook or a clearly scoped action item to produce one within the follow-up window.
- Reduce mean time to first action (MTTFA) for recurring failure modes by providing validated operator procedures.
- Maintain a living library of runbooks with versioning, ownership, test records, and a quarterly verification cadence.

Scope

Applies to platform services owned by the eng-platform org including but not limited to: routing-service, batching-engine, kv-prefix-cache, runtime-gateway, and region-failover. Does not replace product-facing runbooks maintained by individual product teams (those live in their team spaces but should follow the same templates).

When to run this playbook

- After every incident with severity >= Sev2.
- When a change introduces a new operational surface (new autoscaler, new cache sharding scheme, new quantized runtime).
- During scheduled knowledge-transfer sprints (quarterly).

Stakeholders and responsibilities

- Incident Lead: Owns the conversion of the retrospective findings into a draft runbook within 5 business days.
- Service Owner: Validates technical accuracy and assigns an owner for ongoing maintenance.
- Platform Operator (Operator Author): Formalizes steps, produces test scripts, and executes dry-runs.
- Oncall Manager: Schedules tabletop/test windows and ensures runbook is included in oncall playbooks.
- Documentation Reviewer(s): Approve content for publication in the runbook library.

Key Definitions

- Runbook: A step-by-step operational document that an operator can follow to mitigate or recover from a known failure mode.
- Testable Runbook: A runbook with automated or manual verification steps that can be executed in a failure-injection or replay environment.
- Coverage: Percentage of Sev2+ incidents that have an associated runbook or active-creation ticket.

Procedure (ordered)

1) Incident classification and triage (Day 0–1)
   - Incident Lead tags the postmortem with label: postmortem/runbook-required if the issue is repeatable, not previously documented, or requires multi-step operator action.
   - Create a parent JIRA ticket in project PLAT-OPS: type=Documentation, priority=Highest, summary="Runbook: <service> — <short-title>". Link to the incident and retrospective artifacts.

2) Drafting the runbook (Day 1–5)
   - Use the official runbook template (see Appendix) and store in Confluence path runbooks/<service>/<major-version>/<slug>. Example slug: runbook/routing-service/v3/prefix-cache-warmup.
   - Include: problem statement, symptoms, pre-req checks, impact scope, mitigation steps (with safety checks), rollback steps, post-restore verification, and owner contact information.
   - Add explicit SLO context: e.g., "service P99 latency target: <120ms; error rate target: <0.05%". If the incident consumed >20% error budget, mark runbook as high-priority.

3) Operator validation and tabletop (Day 3–10)
   - Operator Author performs a dry-run in staging or in a controlled chaos workspace. Attach test logs to the runbook page.
   - Run a 30-minute tabletop with the oncall rotation for the affected region: agenda in Appendix. Record minutes and update the runbook.
   - If a step requires privileged access (KMS/HSM or node-level), document exact RBAC roles and the least-privilege escalation path.

4) Publication and assignment (Day 5–14)
   - Documentation Reviewer(s) check for clarity, safety, and completeness. Approved runbooks are moved from draft -> published and tagged runbook:published.
   - Assign a recurring quarterly owner check (Confluence task with assignee = Service Owner).

5) Procedural automation and integration (Day 7–30)
   - Create automation where possible (CLI snippets, runbooks-as-code modules, or a small Playbook script). Host artifacts in platform-ops/runbook-scripts repo.
   - Add link to PagerDuty escalation PD-Platform-Primary and Slack incident channel #platform-ops. Add a Notify step that includes the JIRA parent ticket ID.

6) Ongoing maintenance and verification (Quarterly)
   - Owners must re-run testable steps at least once per quarter or after any major service release. Maintain a verification log on the runbook page.
   - If a runbook fails a verification run, create a remediation ticket and mark runbook:stale until fixed.

Templates and conventions

- File and page naming: runbook/{service}/{major-version}/{short-title}; example: runbook/kv-prefix-cache/v2/eviction-rebalance.
- Minimum content sections (must be present): Summary, Symptoms, Preconditions, Mitigation Steps, Verification, Rollback, Owner and Contact, Change Log, Test Log, Related Incidents.
- Tone and voice: imperative, concise, and free of speculative debugging notes. Keep heuristics in an appendix, not in the main mitigation steps.

Runbook Skeleton (copy into new runbook)

---- START RUNBOOK TEMPLATE ----
Title: <service> — <short-title>
Summary: One-sentence description of the failure mode and impact.
Symptoms: Bullet list of observable indicators (metrics, logs, error messages).
Preconditions: Checks to run before taking action (region, credentials, current load).
Mitigation steps: Numbered, safety-claused commands and expected observables after each step.
Verification: Exact metrics/log queries and thresholds to confirm service health.
Rollback: Reverse steps with precise condition checks.
Owner: Name, pager (PD escalation), Slack handle.
Test log: Date, executor, environment, result, artifacts (links).
Change log: Date, author, summary of changes.
Related incidents: List of retrospective links.
---- END RUNBOOK TEMPLATE ----

Operational quality gates and acceptance criteria

- Runbook created within 7 business days for Sev2+ incidents (measured by PLAT-OPS ticket creation timestamp).
- At least one successful dry-run or automated test recorded before publication.
- Oncall MTTFA for matching incidents decreases by 20% within two quarters of runbook publication (if runbook addresses the dominant fault class).
- Quarterly verification pass rate >= 90% across published runbooks.

Metrics and KPIs to track (dashboard suggestions)

- runbook.coverage.percent: (Sev2+ incidents with runbooks / total Sev2+ incidents) * 100. Target: >= 95%.
- runbook.test.pass_rate: Ratio of verification runs passing to total verification attempts. Target: >= 90%.
- oncall.mttfa: Median time between pager trigger and first mitigation action by oncall. Target: reduce by 20% after runbook publication.
- runbook.age: Time since last verification. Alert when > 90 days.

Suggested dashboard widgets (Grafana)

- Single line: runbook.coverage.percent (30-day)
- Heatmap: runbook.age by service
- Bar: runbook.test.pass_rate by owner_team
- Table: Open PLAT-OPS runbook tickets with due dates and owners

Owner ship and lifecycle

- Creation: Incident Lead -> creates draft and JIRA ticket.
- Primary owner: Service Owner (responsible for content accuracy).
- Operational author: Platform Operator (maintains step-level accuracy and test logs).
- Reviewer: Documentation Reviewer (publishes and validates readability).
- Archivist: Oncall Manager (marks runbook stale/archived after two consecutive failed verifications or after service deprecation).

Oncall and tabletop agenda (30 minutes)

- 0–5m: Context and symptoms recap (Incident Lead)
- 5–10m: Walkthrough of the runbook mitigation steps (Operator Author)
- 10–20m: Simulated execution and decision points discussion (all attendees)
- 20–25m: Ownership, permissions, and automation gaps
- 25–30m: Action items, ticketing, and verification assignment

Change control, versioning and auditing

- Each published runbook page must include a Change Log table at the top with entries: date, author, change-summary, and a link to the PLAT-OPS ticket that triggered the change.
- Maintain a runbook:git-ref property with the SHA of any scripts or playbooks used during mitigation.
- Periodic audit: Oncall Manager will run an automated query for runbook.age > 90d and produce a weekly remediation queue.

Failure modes and special cases

- If a failure mode is only reproducible under high regional load, add explicit throttling thresholds and a step to coordinate cross-region traffic shaping.
- For incidents caused by model swaps or quantization regressions, include a tie-in to model-release notes and evasion criteria (link to eng-serving-runtime/model-onboarding pages).

Appendix: Examples and snippets

- Example CLI snippet to add a Confluence skeleton (runbooks-as-code):

  git clone git@github.com:redwood/platform-ops.git
  cd platform-ops/runbook-templates
  ./create_runbook.sh --service routing-service --version v3 --slug prefix-cache-warmup

- Example verification query (PromQL):

  # Verify P99 latency under 120ms for the last 5m
  histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(routing_service_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le)) < 0.12

- Table: runbook lifecycle states (described):

  - draft: Created, not yet validated
  - published: Validated and approved
  - stale: Failed verification or pending update after a release
  - archived: Service decommissioned or runbook superseded

Related pages and links

- Platform operator handbook: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/platform-operator-handbook-degraded-kv-prefix-cache-2026
- Model onboarding guidelines: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/model-onboarding/standards
- PLAT-OPS JIRA project: PLAT-OPS (use component=runbook)
- PagerDuty escalation: PD-Platform-Primary
- Slack channel: #platform-ops

Appendix: Quick checklist for Incident Leads

- [ ] Tag retrospective "postmortem/runbook-required" when applicable
- [ ] Create PLAT-OPS ticket linking to retrospective and assign priority
- [ ] Ensure Operator Author is identified and booked for a tabletop
- [ ] Verify a dry-run is scheduled before publication
- [ ] Confirm owner and quarterly verification date are set
